newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kone sees European lift upgrade boom.
newsitem.headline: Kone sees European lift upgrade boom.

text.p: Finnish elevator maker Kone Oy said in a statement on Monday the group's net sales in lift modernisation could double by the year 2000 from 1.5 billion markka per year currently due to an expected boom in Europe.
"Expectations that the Kone group's 1.5 billion markka modernisation business will double by the year 2000 are quite justified," Kone president Anssi Soila said.
The statement quoted an interview with Soila in a Kone newsletter.
In Europe, hundreds of thousands of existing elevators do not meet current safety standards, Soila said, adding that EU legislation may help boost demand for elevator modernisation.

The EU commission has said the operational safety of elevators should be at the same level throughout the EU area, he said. For example, he said nearly half a million elevators in Europe have cages but no doors.
"The implementation of all EU commission recommendations is expected to create a 150 billion markka modernisation market for the European elevator industry," he said.
Of the 430,000 elevators under maintenance contract with Kone, 75 percent are in the EU area, Soila said, adding these elevators were on average 20 years old.
"Regardless of how well they have been maintained, elevators of this age do not fulfil today's requirements without renewal of components," he said.
